mainTopic: A daughter's dowry (פרנסה) from her father's estate: equal division, losing it by maturing or marrying, the role of protest, and how it differs from a תנאי כתובה
overview: The גמרא first explains רבי's rule that daughters 'divide equally': it applies only when they all marry at the same time, and this supports רב מתנה. Next, a ברייתא records an argument about a daughter who matured or married. Everyone agrees she loses her food support (מזונות). רבי says she keeps her dowry (פרנסה), and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says she loses that too. רב נחמן rules like רבי, and רבא challenges him from the משנה about an orphan girl. The answer is that she keeps her dowry if she protests, and silence counts as giving it up. Another ברייתא of רבי confirms this. רבא's own ruling that she sometimes need not protest is explained by whether her brothers still feed her. Finally, רב הונא quotes רבי that a dowry is not like a תנאי כתובה. After two rejected explanations, the גמרא shows the real difference: a father can cancel his daughters' dowry but not their food.

steps.title: Why should the daughters split their dowries equally?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's ruling that the daughters divide equally, since each daughter already took her own proper share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each and every daughter takes her own share! So why should they divide equally?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the last part of רבי's ruling, which said the daughters 'divide equally.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ruled that each daughter, when she marries, takes a tenth of whatever is left of the estate. Each sister has then already received what she is owed. Making them pool it and split it again seems to make no sense.

phrases.english: Each and every one
phrases.notes: This is about רבי's earlier rule: each daughter, when she marries, takes a tenth of what is left of the estate.

phrases.english: takes her own [share]! (So why divide equally?)

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the daughters 'divide equally'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each daughter already took the correct share at her own wedding, there is no reason to split everything again.

steps.title: Equal division applies only when they all marry at once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי meant they divide equally only when all the daughters marry at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: if they all come to be married at the same time, they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting the 'divide equally' rule to one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the daughters marry at different times, each one takes a tenth of what is left at her own wedding. When they all marry together, nobody gets more just because her wedding happened to come first, so they split equally.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If they all come to be married at the same time,
they divide equally.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Equal division seemed to apply even when the weddings are spread out, which would cancel the tenth-by-tenth system.
steps.terutzMaskana: Equal division applies only when all the daughters marry at the same time.

steps.title: This supports רב מתנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this explanation matches a ruling of רב מתנה about daughters who marry at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב מתנה, who said: if they all come to be married at the same time, they take one tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב מתנה's statement because it fits the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה also ruled about daughters who all marry at the same time. That matches the new reading of רבי, so the ברייתא supports him. His wording about 'one tenth' will be questioned in the next step.

phrases.english: This supports רב מתנה.
For רב מתנה said:
If they all come to be married at the same time,
they take one tenth.

steps.raayaObject: רב מתנה's ruling about daughters who marry at the same time
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא as explained in step 2

steps.title: Could they all share only one tenth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב מתנה's wording, since it sounds like all the daughters together share a single tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think they take just one tenth between all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב מתנה's words cannot be taken literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One tenth' sounds like all the sisters together get only a single tenth of the estate. That would leave each of them with less than she would get by marrying separately, which cannot be right.

phrases.english: Could you think it means one tenth [for all of them]?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the daughters would lose out just because they married at the same time.

steps.title: Each takes a tenth, all in equal measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב מתנה: each daughter takes a tenth, and all the shares are made equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: they take a tenth as one, meaning everyone in the same equal amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא corrects how to read רב מתנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אחד' does not mean one tenth for everyone together. It should be read as 'כאחד', 'as one': each sister takes her tenth, and the amounts are evened out so every sister ends up with the same.
steps.whatToRemember: When all the daughters marry at the same time, each gets a tenth-share and the shares are made equal. Nobody gains just because her wedding came first.

phrases.english: Rather: they take a tenth as one.
phrases.notes: Each sister takes a tenth, and they all end up with the same amount.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: They all share a single tenth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each takes a tenth, made equal across all the sisters.

steps.title: Does a daughter who matured or married lose her dowry?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: everyone agrees she loses מזונות. רבי says she keeps her פרנסה, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says she loses that too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: daughters, whether they matured before marrying or married before maturing, lose their food support but not their dowry. These are רבי's words. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: they lose their dowry too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about what happens to a daughter's rights once she matures or marries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food support (מזונות) from the estate is only for a young, unmarried daughter, so both of these daughters lose it. The argument is about the dowry (פרנסה): רבי says the right stays, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it ends as well.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מזונות (food) with פרנסה (dowry). Both sides agree she loses מזונות. They argue only about פרנסה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: The daughters,
whether they matured before they married
or they married before they matured,
have lost their food support
but have not lost their dowry; these are the words of רבי.
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
They have lost their dowry as well.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both lose מזונות. רבי: they keep their פרנסה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: they lose their פרנסה too.

steps.title: How to save the dowry: marry before maturing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a daughter keeps her dowry by making sure she marries before she matures.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should they do? They 'hire' husbands for themselves, and then they take out their dowry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives practical advice for daughters who would otherwise lose their dowry under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If maturing before marriage ends the dowry right, the only way to keep it is to marry while still young. The daughters work hard to find husbands in time, and then they collect their dowry.

phrases.english: What do they do?
They hire husbands for themselves,
phrases.notes: Not literally hiring. It means they make every effort to get married before they mature.

phrases.english: and they take out their dowry for themselves.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a daughter keeps her פרנסה by marrying before she matures.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reports in the name of רב הונא that the הלכה follows רבי: an adult daughter keeps her dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me the הלכה follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a ruling on the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ruling, a daughter who matured before marrying can still collect her dowry from the estate. This ruling is the target of the challenge in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: רב נחמן said: הונא told me:
The הלכה follows רבי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר לִי הוּנָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי: a daughter who matured keeps her פרנסה.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב נחמן from the משנה about the orphan girl
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה that lets a minor orphan girl later claim her full dowry. He infers that an adult who agreed to a small dowry gave up the rest, which seems to go against רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: an orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off with her agreement, and wrote her a dowry of a hundred or fifty זוז, can, once she grows up, collect from them what she should have been given. The reason is that she was a minor. But if she were an adult, she would have given up the rest!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling using a careful reading of a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the orphan claim the rest of her dowry only because she married as a minor. That suggests an adult who agreed to a small dowry gave up the rest. This seems to fit רבי שמעון בן אלעזר rather than רבי.

phrases.english: רבא challenged רב נחמן:

phrases.aramaic: יְתוֹמָה שֶׁהִשִּׂיאַתָּה אִמָּהּ אוֹ אַחֶיהָ מִדַּעְתָּהּ,
phrases.english: An orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off with her consent,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתְבוּ לָהּ בְּמֵאָה אוֹ בַּחֲמִשִּׁים זוּז,
phrases.english: and they wrote her a dowry of a hundred or fifty זוז,
she can, once she grows up,

phrases.aramaic: לְהוֹצִיא מִיָּדָם מַה שֶּׁרָאוּי לְהִנָּתֵן לָהּ.
phrases.english: collect from them what is fit to be given to her.
The reason is that she was a minor;
but if she were an adult, she gave it up!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the orphan her full dowry only because she was a minor. That implies an adult loses it, which fits רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and not רבי.

steps.title: Protesting versus staying silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves רבא's challenge. רבי's ruling is about a daughter who protests, and the inference from the משנה is about one who does not protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this case is where she protests, and that case is where she does not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's question by saying the two sources are talking about two different adult daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says an adult daughter keeps her dowry. That is true when she protests and insists on her full share. The inference from the משנה, that she gave up the rest, applies only when she stayed silent and accepted less.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
This one... that one; each source is about a different case
She protests; she objects and insists on her rights

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where she protests,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רבי's ruling that an adult daughter keeps her dowry.

phrases.english: that one is where she does not protest.
phrases.notes: "That one" is the inference רבא drew from the משנה, that she gave up the rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — דְּמַחַאי, הָא — דְּלָא מַחַאי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): protest versus silence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה shows that any adult daughter loses her dowry, which would go against רבי
steps.terutzMaskana: An adult daughter keeps her dowry only if she protests. Silence counts as giving it up.

steps.title: Support: otherwise רבי would contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the answer. Without the protest distinction, another ברייתא of רבי would seem to say that an adult daughter gets no dowry at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. Otherwise רבי contradicts רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי says a daughter who is fed by the brothers takes a tenth of the property. If she is fed, yes. If she is not fed, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that the protest distinction must be right. Without it, רבי would contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In another ברייתא, רבי gives a dowry to a daughter who is "fed by the brothers." Only a minor gets fed, so this implies an adult gets no dowry. That clashes with רבי's ruling in step 6 unless we split the cases by protest and silence.

keyTerms.meaning: This also stands to reason; it introduces support for an answer
One statement of רבי contradicts another statement of רבי
One-tenth of the estate, the daughter's dowry share
Is fed or supported from the estate

phrases.english: This also stands to reason,
for if so, Rabbi would contradict Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if we did not split the cases by protest and silence.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi says:
A daughter who is fed by the brothers
takes a tenth of the property.
If she is fed, yes,
if she is not fed, no.
phrases.notes: An adult daughter loses her food support (step 6), so "not fed" means an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִם כֵּן, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי אַדְּרַבִּי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי gives a dowry only to a daughter who is fed, which implies an adult gets none

steps.title: Conclusion: it depends on protest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי's two statements fit together. One is about a daughter who protests and the other is about one who stays silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, must we not conclude from this: this one is where she protests, and that one is where she does not protest? Conclude from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the matter. רבי's two rulings fit together because one is about protest and the other is about silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling that she keeps her dowry is about an adult daughter who protests. The ruling that she gets nothing is about one who stays silent. This both resolves רבי against himself and confirms the answer to רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that; it introduces the only workable explanation
Learn from this; we can conclude it

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי, an adult orphan daughter keeps her עישור נכסים only if she protests. If she stays silent and accepts less, she has given up the rest.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not conclude from this:
this one is where she protests, that one is where she does not protest.
Conclude from this.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Protest keeps the dowry and silence gives it up. רבי's statements are consistent.

steps.title: When does she need to protest?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes רבא's own ruling through רב אדא בר אהבה. A daughter who only matured, or only married, does not need to protest. A daughter who both matured and married does need to protest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: רב אדא בר אהבה told us in your name: If she matured, she does not need to protest. If she married, she does not need to protest. If she matured and married, she needs to protest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a ruling that defines exactly when a daughter must protest to keep her dowry rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maturing alone does not cost her anything. Marrying alone does not cost her anything either. Only when both happen does her silence count as giving up the dowry. This seems to clash with steps 10–12, where a girl who only matured or only married needed to protest. The next step raises exactly that problem.

keyTerms.meaning: She matured; she reached full adulthood
To protest; to object out loud

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying that maturing alone requires a protest. According to this report, she must protest only when both conditions are true: she matured and she married.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַן רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מִשְּׁמָךְ:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava told us in your name:
If she matured, she does not need to protest,
if she married, she does not need to protest.
If she matured and married, she needs to protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: אֲמַר לַן רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מִשְּׁמָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ruling of רבא about when a protest is needed, which seems to conflict with the protest answer of steps 10–12 and is challenged in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A protest is needed only if she both matured and married. Maturing alone, or marrying alone, does not require one.

steps.title: Does רבא contradict what he accepted from רב נחמן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's ruling from Step 13 using the earlier back-and-forth he had with רב נחמן about the יתומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But רבא challenged רב נחמן with the case of the orphan girl, and רב נחמן answered him: one case is where she protests, the other is where she does not protest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבא could really have said that a daughter who only matured, or only married, does not need to protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 9–10, רבא challenged רב נחמן with the יתומה, and the answer was that רבי's ruling (a daughter who matured before marrying, or married before maturing, keeps her dowry) holds only when she protests. So under that answer, a girl who only matured or only married must protest. That clashes with רבא's ruling in Step 13, where such a girl does not need to protest.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say? (an opening that questions a quoted ruling)

phrases.english: Did Rava really say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן יְתוֹמָה,
phrases.english: But Rava challenged Rav Nachman with "an orphan girl,"
phrases.notes: This is the משנה רבא raised back in Step 9, about the minor orphan who was married off.

phrases.english: and he answered him:
this is where she protests,
that is where she does not protest!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָא אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 13 using the answer he accepted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a girl who only matured, or only married, does not need to protest
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer to רבא's own challenge made רבי's cases of a girl who only matured or only married depend on protest. So for her silence does matter, which goes against רבא's ruling that she need not protest.

steps.title: It depends on whether her brothers still feed her
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings deal with different cases: a girl still fed by the brothers, and a girl who is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where she is still being fed by them. That ruling is where she is not being fed by them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no real contradiction, because the two rulings deal with different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brothers still feed her, she is embarrassed to protest, so her silence does not mean she gave anything up. That is רבא's ruling. If they no longer feed her, she has no reason to keep quiet, so silence does count. That is the case רב נחמן answered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: A daughter's silence counts as giving up her dowry only when she is no longer being fed by her brothers.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where she is being fed by them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the brothers who inherited the estate. While they feed her, she feels too awkward to protest.

phrases.english: that is where she is not being fed by them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — דְּקָא מִיתַּזְנָא מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא contradicts the answer he accepted from רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's ruling is about a girl still fed by the brothers. רב נחמן's answer is about a girl who is not fed by them.

steps.title: רב הונא: פרנסה is not like a תנאי כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רבי that the dowry is not treated like the conditions written into the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי: Dowry is not like a condition of the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic: רבי says that a daughter's dowry is not like the conditions of the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conditions of the כתובה include the daughters' food after their father dies. רבי says the dowry follows different rules, but he does not say how. The גמרא will try to work that out next.

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter's dowry, paid from her father's estate
Conditions the court builds into every כתובה, such as the daughters' food

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rabbi said:
Dowry is not like a condition of the ketubah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how the dowry differs from the conditions of the כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dowry follows different rules from the conditions of the כתובה.

steps.title: What does "not like a תנאי כתובה" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what way the dowry differs from the conditions of the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "is not like a condition of the כתובה" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי meant. This question sets up the attempts to explain him that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's statement does not say what the difference is. So the גמרא will test possible differences one at a time.

phrases.english: What does "is not like a condition of the ketubah" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב הונא's statement in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way the dowry differs from the conditions of the כתובה

steps.title: First try: collecting from sold land, which is already known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the difference is about collecting from land that was already sold, but rejects this because everyone already knows it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say that dowry can be collected from mortgaged property that was sold, but a condition of the כתובה cannot, what is רבי teaching us? We see it happen every day: the court collects from such property for dowry, but not for food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible difference and then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the dowry can be taken even from land the heirs already sold, while the daughters' food cannot. But courts already do exactly this every day. So רבי would not need to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Mortgaged property that was later sold to others
What is he teaching us? (what is new here?)
It happens every day; it is already common practice

phrases.english: If we say:
that for dowry she collects from mortgaged property that was sold,
but for a condition of the ketubah she does not collect from mortgaged property that was sold,
what is he teaching us?
But it happens every day
that they collect for dowry,
phrases.notes: "Collect" here means taking from property the heirs have already sold to a buyer.

phrases.english: but they do not collect for food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא: דְּאִילּוּ פַּרְנָסָה — טָרְפָא מִמְּשַׁעְבְּדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to Step 17 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the difference is about collecting from sold property
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Courts already do this every day, so רבי's statement would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Second try: collecting from movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the difference is that dowry can be collected from movable property, but the conditions of the כתובה only from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference is that dowry can be collected even from movable property, while a condition of the כתובה is collected from land but not from movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new explanation of רבי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the difference is about what kind of property can be used to pay. The suggestion is that dowry can come from movable property too, while the daughters' food can come only from land.

phrases.english: Rather, that for dowry
she collects even from movable property,
but a condition of the ketubah she collects from land,
and from movable property she does not collect.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, דְּאִילּוּ פַּרְנָסָה גָּבְיָא נָמֵי מִמִּטַּלְטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in Step 18 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dowry can be collected from movable property, but the conditions of the כתובה only from land.

steps.title: רבי lets both be collected from movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the second explanation, because a ברייתא shows that רבי lets food be collected from movable property too.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי, both can be collected from either kind of property. As a ברייתא teaches: whether it is property that has a guarantee or property that has no guarantee, the court collects from it for the food of the wife and the daughters. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the second explanation using a ברייתא in רבי's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that רבי lets the court collect the wife's and daughters' food from both land and movable property. Food is a condition of the כתובה, so for רבי it is collected from movable property just like the dowry. That means this cannot be the difference רבי meant.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that; both of them
Property that has a guarantee, meaning land
Property with no guarantee, meaning movable objects

steps.confusionAlert: Here "both" means both kinds of property, land and movable property. It does not mean both kinds of payment.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi, from both this and that she certainly collects,
as it is taught in a baraita:
whether property that has a guarantee
or property that has no guarantee,
they collect from it for the food of the wife and the daughters,
these are the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation offered in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the conditions of the כתובה cannot be collected from movable property
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that רבי lets the court collect the wife's and daughters' food from movable property too.

steps.title: So what does רבי's rule really mean?
steps.stepSummary: Both suggested explanations failed, so the גמרא asks again what the difference between a dowry and the conditions of the כתובה is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'a dowry is not like the conditions of the כתובה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Both earlier explanations were pushed away, so the גמרא asks again for the meaning of רבי's statement. This line sets up the real answer, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the גמרא is dropping the earlier ideas about sold land and movable property. It still needs some real difference between a dowry and the conditions of the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what? It drops earlier answers and asks again.
Dowry, the money given to a daughter when she marries
The conditions the בית דין built into every כתובה, such as feeding the daughters

phrases.english: Rather, what is the meaning of
'A dowry is not like the conditions of the כתובה'?
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's quote from רבי, back in step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 20 rejected the second explanation, so the גמרא reopens the question from step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference makes a dowry unlike the conditions of the כתובה?

steps.title: A father can cancel the dowry but not his daughters' food
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from a ברייתא. A father's instruction that his daughters should not be fed from his estate is ignored. His instruction that they should not get a dowry from it is followed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to what a ברייתא teaches. If a man says, 'My daughters should not be fed from my property,' we do not listen to him. If he says, 'My daughters should not get a dowry from my property,' we do listen to him, because a dowry is not like the conditions of the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. A father can stop his daughters from getting a dowry from his estate, but he cannot stop them from getting food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding the daughters after the father dies is one of the conditions of the כתובה, so it is a fixed duty and his words cannot cancel it. A dowry is not one of those conditions, so if the father says not to give it, his wish is followed. That is the difference רבי meant.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to what a ברייתא teaches
They should be fed (from מְזוֹנוֹת, food and support)
We listen to him, so his instruction is followed

steps.whatToRemember: Food for the daughters is a condition of the כתובה, so the father cannot cancel it. A dowry is not a condition of the כתובה, so the father can cancel it.
steps.confusionAlert: יִזּוֹנוּ (food) and יִתְפַּרְנְסוּ (dowry) sound alike but mean different things here. The whole rule depends on keeping them apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the real halachic difference between a daughter's food and her dowry. It tells us which one the father's instruction can take away.

phrases.english: It refers to what is taught in a ברייתא:
One who says, 'His daughters should not be fed from his property'
we do not listen to him.
But if he says, 'His daughters should not get a dowry from his property'
we do listen to him,
because a dowry is not like the conditions of the כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is that a father can cancel his daughters' dowry but not their food.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי's statement means that a dowry, unlike the daughters' food, can be cancelled by the father's instruction.
